text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-01: I refetched all 17 relevant UniProt sequences and ran exact plus longest-common-substring searches myself. Every enumerated instance holds: CVDRENPVEWVRAC vs BDNF P23560 — absent, longest common substring 3 ('EWV'); EPKHVNCDRENP vs NGF P01138 — absent, LCS 2; GRLVGHPWECDR vs TREM2 Q9NZC2 — absent, LCS 2; SEAEFRLFRDVW vs CHRNA7 P36544 — absent, LCS 3; CKCHGMSGSCSTK vs WNT3A P56704 — absent, LCS 5 ('CKCHG'); DEETGEFLFQLP vs NFE2L2 Q16236 — absent, LCS 8 ('DEETGEFL'), against the genuine DEETGEFLPIQP which I confirmed at Q16236 residues 77-88; VRACPTGKCEGL vs NTRK2 Q16620 — absent, LCS 4. The 'Loop-5' point is also right: neurotrophins have four beta-hairpin loops. The TrkB domain architecture claim is right too — Q16620 UniProt features list LRRNT, LRR, LRRCT, Ig-like C2-type 1 (197-282), Ig-like C2-type 2 (295-365) and kinase (538-807); no EGF-like repeat anywhere. WHERE THE FINDING OVERREACHES: the title asserts 'every claimed natural-sequence provenance is false.' That universal is refuted by two counterexamples in the same dataset. (a) app.js:225 'GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG' is an EXACT substring of GSK3B P49841 at residues 3-34, and it genuinely contains Ser9 — so the README:70 'GSK-3beta Ser9 Mimetic' provenance is real, not invented. (b) KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM is an exact substring of APP P05067 (Abeta16-35) — which the reviewer credits in the overall assessment but the finding title contradicts. The enumerated evidence is entirely sound; only the universal quantifier in the title is wrong. Correction: Retitle to the scope actually demonstrated: 'Nine of the claimed natural-sequence provenances cannot be reproduced against the cited UniProt accession.' Two provenances ARE genuine and must be excluded from any deletion sweep: GSK3B P49841 residues 3-34 (app.js:225) and APP P05067 Abeta16-35 (app.js:277, README:77). Also fix the off-by-one in the worked example inside required_fix: 'Nrf2 76-88, Q16236' is 13 residues, LDEETGEFLPIQP, not the 12-mer LDEETGEFLPIQ given (that is 76-87). Finally, the assertion that the recurring Cys ladder is 'EGF-like-repeat architecture' is a structural inference I could not confirm by any database hit; it is not load-bearing (the absence from TrkB is independently proven) and should be softened or dropped.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-02: I extracted all 25 sequence fields programmatically and grouped them. Exactly four sequences appear twice, at exactly the cited lines and exactly the cited lengths: the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG at app.js:153 and 247; the 31-mer CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH at 173 and 371; the 41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC at 195 and 319; the 37-mer VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH at 205 and 361. The paired affinities and target strings are as quoted. The finding is correct and, if anything, understated on two axes I checked and the reviewer did not. FIRST, the thermodynamic inconsistency is not confined to the AChE pair — it is universal. Recomputing dG = RT ln(Kd) at 298.15 K (RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol) for all 25 entries, every stated dG is more negative than its stated Kd permits, by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol, with no exception. SECOND, the same molecules also appear in AF3_CANDIDATES carrying a THIRD, different dG and a different pLDDT: the 36-mer is dG -12.6 / pLDDT 92.8 at app.js:131, -16.2 / 94.8 at app.js:156, and -17.5 / 94.3 at app.js:250; the 41-mer is -12.1 / 90.7 at app.js:134, -16.5 / 93.2 at app.js:198, -15.7 / 92.8 at app.js:322; the 45-mer at app.js:132 is assigned 'NMDA GluN2B NTD' while the identical sequence at app.js:215 is assigned GluN2A. Three values for one molecule is stronger evidence than two. Correction: Arithmetic nit: Kd = 0.65 nM gives dG = -12.53 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, not -12.4 as stated (Kd = 2.1 nM -> -11.84 is correct). Scope correction: report the inconsistency as systematic across all 25 entries (discrepancy 3.85-5.73 kcal/mol, n = 25, zero exceptions) rather than as a property of one duplicate pair, and add the AF3_CANDIDATES cross-list triples above. Also note that the ZO-1 pairing is even worse than stated: ZO-1 is not in the platform at all as a sequence-verified target — the peptide assigned to 'ZO-1/Occludin (Arg220, Asp310)' at app.js:372 is the same corrupted WNT3A fragment.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MOLBIO-03: I tested every residue myself against both accessions in mature numbering. Human AChE P22303 (signal 1-31, offset +31): position 84 = Glu, 330 = Val, 121 = Gly, 279 = Gln — none is the claimed residue. Torpedo AChE P04058 (signal 1-21, offset +21): 84 = Trp, 330 = Phe, 121 = Tyr, 279 = Trp — all four match exactly. So the CAS list is unambiguously Torpedo numbering. The PAS list is unambiguously human: P22303 mature 286 = Trp, 72 = Tyr, 341 = Tyr, 74 = Asp, all correct. The two are welded into one string at app.js:154, exactly as claimed, and app.js:12 lists Torpedo Trp279 while app.js:72 and app.js:154 list human Trp286 — the same PAS tryptophan presented as two sites. The proposed human equivalents also check out: P22303 mature 86 = Trp, 337 = Tyr, 124 = Tyr, 295 = Phe, 297 = Phe, triad 203 = Ser / 334 = Glu / 447 = His; Torpedo mature 70 = Tyr, 72 = Asp, 334 = Tyr. The Torpedo Phe330 -> human Tyr337 caveat is correct and is the trap a naive renumbering would fall into. I confirmed the salt-bridge/cation-pi contradiction by reading app.js:12 and app.js:15 directly: line 12 says 'CAS Salt Bridge', line 15 says 'cation-pi interactions' for the same Trp84/Phe330 contact. Aromatic side chains cannot form salt bridges. Sussman et al., Science 1991;253:872-9 (PMID 1678899) verified via PubMed esummary; PDB 1VOT verified via RCSB as AChE/huperzine A, Raves M.L., Nat Struct Biol 1997. Correction: None. Every residue identity, the species assignment, the equivalence mapping, and both citations verified independently.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-04: Text verified verbatim at app.js:153-158 and 247-252, including 'Completely blocks acetylcholine degradation ... elevating synaptic ACh levels by +350%' and 'Seizure Index: 0.01 | Peripheral Side Effects: None', plus README:100 'Negligible'. The peptide characterisation is exact: I counted the 36-mer and get 9 Lys, 4 Arg, 4 Glu, 0 Asp — net formal charge +9 — and 4 Trp, precisely as claimed. The steric argument is sound: the AChE gorge is ~20 A deep and narrow, and fasciculin-2 is the definitive precedent that a peptide-class ligand caps the PAS and occludes the gorge mouth without reaching the catalytic serine. The pharmacological inversion is the strongest part of the finding and is correct: near-complete AChE inhibition is the mechanism of organophosphate/carbamate cholinergic crisis, and the platform asserts maximal target engagement with zero on-target toxicity, which is self-contradictory for this enzyme. The donepezil anchor is verified verbatim — I pulled the Rogers & Friedhoff abstract (PMID 8915035), which states 'A plateau of inhibition (76-84%) was reached at plasma donepezil concentrations > 50 ng/ml.' Inestrosa et al., Neuron 1996;16:881-91 (PMID 8608006) verified. CITATION ERROR: PDB 1FSS is 'ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE COMPLEXED WITH FASCICULIN-II', primary citation Harel M. et al., Structure 1995 — not Bourne. Bourne et al. 1995 is the mouse AChE-fasciculin structure (Cell), PDB 1MAH. The reviewer's own literature-list entry for 1FSS wisely gives no author; the inline attribution in MOLBIO-04 must be corrected or the finding carries a misattributed structure. Correction: Attribute PDB 1FSS to Harel et al., Structure 1995 (verified via RCSB), not to Bourne et al. If Bourne is wanted, cite it as the separate mouse AChE-Fas2 complex (PDB 1MAH). Also temper the harm framing: 'the clearest path to physical harm' overstates the exposure of a private static web page with no dosing calculator; the defensible statement is that the design objective itself is inverted and would misdirect candidate selection. Minor scope note: B4 (app.js:275-282) is not really an AChE ligand at all — its peptide is Abeta16-35 fused to GRLVGHPW — so 'reclassify B4 as PAS-directed' is generous; it should be flagged as having no AChE-binding element.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-05: Verified residue by residue against NTRK2 Q16620. Full-length numbering: 298 = Asp (correct), 342 = Tyr (correct), 319 = Tyr not Glu, 315 = Leu not Thr, 312 = Lys not Val, 333 = Lys not Leu. Two of six. I independently tested mature numbering (+31 offset): 298 = Tyr, 319 = Asn, 342 = Gln, 312 = His, 333 = Lys, 315 = Leu — zero of six, so the reviewer is right that this is not a convention artefact. The domain credit is also right: UniProt annotates Ig-like C2-type 2 at 295-365, so 298-342 fall inside d5. The absence of a BDNF-TrkB complex is confirmed by a structured RCSB accession search I ran myself: P23560 (BDNF) appears in exactly two PDB entries, 1B8M and 1BND (both BDNF/NT-3 heterodimers, no receptor), and none of the nine Q16620 entries (1HCF, 1WWB, 2MFQ, 4ASZ, 4AT3, 4AT4, 4AT5, 5MO9, 8OYD) contains BDNF — 8OYD, which a text search surfaces, is the TrkB transmembrane-domain NMR structure. Citations verified: PDB 1WWB (apo human TrkB LBD, Ultsch, J Mol Biol 1999), 1HCF (TrkB-d5 with NT-4/5, Banfield, Structure 2001), 5MO9 (TrkB LBD with Fab); Boltaev et al., Sci Signal 2017;10 (PMID 28831019) abstract retrieved and matches the reviewer's characterisation; Zagrebelsky & Korte, Neural Regen Res 2024;19:29-34 (PMID 37488840) verified. Correction: The rhetorical statistic is wrong and should be deleted: 'Two of six correct is what random guessing constrained to the right domain would give' is false. Random guessing over 20 amino acids gives an expectation of ~0.3 correct out of six, so 2/6 is roughly six-fold ABOVE chance, not at chance. The honest statement is that four of six residue identities are wrong under both numbering conventions, and the two that are right (Asp298, Tyr342) cannot be assumed to be by design. Everything else stands.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MOLBIO-06: Verified against CHRNA7 P36544 in mature numbering (signal 1-22): 188 = Tyr, 149 = Trp, 195 = Tyr — all correct as claimed, and I additionally confirmed 93 = Tyr and 55 = Trp, which is decisive because Tyr93/Trp149/Tyr188/Tyr195 plus complementary-face Trp55 IS the canonical orthosteric aromatic box. So the residues the platform lists for a supposed PAM are the acetylcholine site. CHRM1 P11229: 381 = Tyr, 164 = Trp confirmed, and the orthosteric tyrosine lid partners are all present as claimed (105 = Asp, 106 = Tyr, 404 = Tyr, 408 = Tyr). The desensitisation inversion is the sharpest point and is correct: app.js:199 asserts 'Receptor Desensitization: Low' as a consequence of a PAM label while the listed site is orthosteric, and orthosteric alpha-7 agonism is characterised by rapid profound desensitisation. I retrieved the Marotta et al. abstract (PMID 26211363), which states that the increased potency of ACh with PNU-120596 'is not due to an altered agonist binding site' and implicates gating-interface and transmembrane residues — exactly as the reviewer represents it. Targowska-Duda et al. verified (J Biomol Struct Dyn 37:411-439, PMID 29363414). PDB 4MQT (active M2 with LY2119620, Kruse, Nature 2013) and 5CXV (M1 with tiotropium, Thal, Nature 2016) verified. Correction: Two trivial precision points, neither of which weakens the finding. (i) Targowska-Duda et al. is print-dated 2019 in J Biomol Struct Dyn 37:411-439 (online 2018); cite as 2019 or '2018 online, 2019 print'. (ii) The reviewer calls M1 Trp164 merely 'a real residue' — accurate, but it is a TM4 (4.57) residue that belongs to neither the orthosteric lid nor the canonical extracellular allosteric vestibule, so it is unassigned rather than mislabelled. The Tyr381 argument carries the finding on its own.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-07: Every quoted number verified at the cited line: app.js:148 'LTP +280%', app.js:188 '+310%', app.js:200 '+240%', app.js:240 'doubling cortical information processing speed', app.js:252 '+350%', app.js:334 '+420%'. None carries an assay, referent, species, n, or dispersion — that part is simply true on inspection. The conceptual core is the strongest element and is correct: potentiation saturates and saturated hippocampal LTP impairs rather than improves learning, so 'more LTP' is not a coherent objective. Moser, Krobert, Moser & Morris, Science 1998;281:2038-42 (PMID 9748165), 'Impaired spatial learning after saturation of long-term potentiation', verified by PubMed esummary — title, venue, year, volume and pages all exact. The ambiguity point about '+280%' meaning 180% vs 380% of baseline is a real and standard reviewer objection. However this finding is qualitatively different from MOLBIO-01/02/03/06: it is an 'unsupported-claim' category defect (the reviewer's own label) sitting downstream of a dataset already proven fabricated, and it does not introduce an independent, actionable technical error the way a wrong residue or a wrong species numbering does. Correction: One overstatement to soften: 'beyond the geometric packing limit of the dendritic shaft' is not defensible at the low end. Reported CA1 spine densities span roughly 1-3 per micrometre, and densities of 4-5 per micrometre are observed on some dendritic segments and in synaptopathies, so a 4.1-fold increase is far outside the physiological range and into pathology, but it is not geometrically impossible. Restate as 'far outside any reported physiological range, and in the range associated with spine overproduction in fragile X and related synaptopathies.' The microdialysis framing ('roughly 100-500% of basal') is a fair general characterisation but is offered without a specific citation and should either be cited or given as an order-of-magnitude statement.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MOLBIO-08: All locations verified by direct reading: app.js:109-114 defines the microglia region as 'Microglia (M1/M2 State Polarization)' with action text 'shifting inflammatory M1 microglia to neuroprotective M2 phagocytic states'; app.js:304 repeats it; index.html:186 renders 'Microglia (M1/M2 State)'; README:80-85 as quoted. The naming collision is real and worse than a presentational nuisance: 'MicroTrem2-Agonist-M1' at app.js:297 is a drug named M1 whose stated purpose at app.js:304 is to abolish M1 microglia, while 'BasalM1-PAM-B2' at app.js:255 uses M1 for the muscarinic receptor — three incompatible referents in one dataset, exactly as claimed. Both citations verified by PubMed esummary with exact metadata: Ransohoff RM, 'A polarizing question: do M1 and M2 microglia exist?', Nat Neurosci 2016;19:987-91 (PMID 27459405); Paolicelli RC et al., 'Microglia states and nomenclature: A field at its crossroads', Neuron 2022;110:3458-3483 (PMID 36327895). The scientific substance — that M1/M2 was imported from in vitro macrophage paradigms, that single-cell work resolves a continuum of context-dependent states, and that TREM2-dependent DAM are simultaneously highly activated and beneficial — is standard current consensus and correctly stated. Correction: 'Formally deprecated by the field' is a shade strong as a matter of process — no body formally deprecates nomenclature. The accurate formulation is that a ~90-author field consensus paper (Paolicelli et al. 2022) recommends against the dualistic classification and issues explicit nomenclature guidance, following Ransohoff's 2016 argument that the schema should be discarded. Substance unaffected.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-09: Verified against TREM2 Q9NZC2: position 47 = Arg (correct), 87 = Asp (correct), 112 = Ser NOT Lys — the reviewer is right, and UniProt annotates Ig-like V-type at 29-112, so 112 is indeed the domain boundary. Provenance confirmed: GRLVGHPWECDR is absent from Q9NZC2 with longest common substring 2. The mechanistic argument is sound and standard: TREM2 signals via the ITAM adaptor DAP12 and requires clustering for Src-family trans-phosphorylation and SYK recruitment, so a monovalent 12-mer engaging one Ig domain cannot be an agonist by construction. The clinical citation is the reviewer's most surprising claim and I retrieved the full abstract to check it: Mummery CJ et al., 'The TREM2 agonistic antibody AL002 in early Alzheimer's disease: a phase 2 randomized trial', Nat Med 2026;32:1708-1716 (PMID 41787076) — 381 participants, 1:1:1:1 randomisation, 48-96 weeks, reduced CSF sTREM2 and increased osteopontin, primary CDR-SB endpoint not met at week 96 (all three doses, P > 0.05), and 'the most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events were magnetic resonance imaging changes resembling amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA)', NCT04592874. Every detail the reviewer asserts is verbatim correct. Kober DL et al., eLife 2016;5 (PMID 27995897) verified, and its abstract does state that AD risk variants sit on the surface and impair ligand binding; PDB 5ELI, 5UD7 and 6B8O verified via RCSB (5UD7/6B8O are Sudom et al., J Biol Chem 2018, 6B8O being the WT Ig-like V domain with phosphatidylserine). WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: the Asp87 sub-claim. The reviewer writes that 'Asp87 is acidic, which is hard to reconcile with a ligand surface whose defining property is a basic patch.' D87N is a recognised TREM2 coding variant that maps to precisely the AD-risk functional surface Kober et al. define — a EuropePMC query for TREM2 AND "D87N" returns 91 records — and UniProt annotates ligand-binding residues at 67, 68, 77 and 88, placing Asp87 immediately adjacent to an annotated contact. Asp87 is therefore one of the few residues in the entire platform that is both the right amino acid and on the right surface. Correction: Delete the Asp87 objection and the corresponding clause in required_fix ('justify Asp87 against the published anionic-ligand-binding surface'). Asp87 is correct: it is a genuine surface residue on the Kober functional epitope and the site of the AD-associated D87N variant. As written, the fix would push authors to remove or 'justify' one of the platform's few accurate residue assignments. Keep the Lys112 -> Ser112 correction, the monovalency/DAP12 argument, the provenance failure, and the AL002 addition — all of those verified cleanly.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MOLBIO-10: The credit is fully earned and I re-verified it: KEAP1 Q14145 position 334 = Tyr, 415 = Arg, 483 = Arg, 602 = Ser, and the extended hot-spot set the reviewer names is also exactly right — 380 = Arg, 382 = Asn, 414 = Asn, 508 = Ser, 555 = Ser, 572 = Tyr. Position 151 = Cys confirmed. The Nrf2 motif comparison is exact: Q16236 residues 77-88 are DEETGEFLPIQP against the platform's DEETGEFLFQLP, sharing DEETGEFL and diverging thereafter. The domain-conflation charge is verified by direct reading of index.html:230, which collapses 'Keap1 Cys151 Alkylation / Decoy Binding Nrf2 Dissociation' into one pathway step, welding a BTB-domain covalent event to a Kelch-domain PPI competition. The hinge-and-latch objection is correct and is the strongest design-level point: a monovalent ETGE-only decoy competes at the high-affinity hinge and does not address the DLG latch whose disengagement blocks ubiquitin transfer. All four citations verified by PubMed esummary and RCSB with exact metadata: PDB 2FLU (Kelch-Neh2 complex, Lo S.C., EMBO J 2006); Tong KI et al., Biol Chem 2006;387:1311-20 (PMID 17081101); Shibata T et al., PNAS 2008;105:13568-73 (PMID 18757741); Takaya K et al., Free Radic Biol Med 2012;53:817-27 (PMID 22732183). The Nrf2-activation oncogenicity caveat is a legitimate and commonly-missed requirement for a chronic CNS indication. Correction: None material. One small addition worth making when implementing: the platform's own inconsistency is sharper than stated — app.js:82 assigns Asiatic Acid to 'Keap1 Tyr334, Arg415' (Kelch) while app.js:52 assigns Curcumin to 'Keap1 Cys151' (BTB), and app.js:161-168 fuses a curcumin warhead to a Kelch-binding decoy, so the same conjugate is simultaneously assigned both mechanisms without a linker argument.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MOLBIO-11: I validated every character of all 25 sequences plus the 10 AF3_CANDIDATES fasta fields against the 20-letter standard alphabet. Exactly three entries fail, as claimed: the letter B in CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH at app.js:173 and app.js:371, the same B inside the rank-6 fasta at app.js:130, and app.js:381 whose sequence field is the literal string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. I confirmed by reading initModal3DCanvas (app.js:707-773), renderModalPlddtChart (775-832) and renderModalPaeHeatmap (834-866) that none validates input — all three index charCodeAt directly — so A4 will render a 3D backbone, a pLDDT curve and a PAE matrix from a description string. THE PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG. Aligning the platform 31-mer to WNT3A P56704 from residue 203 (CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP, which I confirmed begins at 203): platform positions 1-18 map to WNT3A 203-220, so the B at platform position 19 aligns to WNT3A Gln221, not Leu. The Leu is at WNT3A 208, which the platform renders as Met at position 6 — the L->M substitution the reviewer themselves correctly identified in MOLBIO-01. Implementing 'correct the B to L, per WNT3A P56704' would write a Leu where the genuine residue is Gln, i.e. replace an invalid character with a wrong one, and it contradicts MOLBIO-01 within the same report. Correction: The B corresponds to WNT3A P56704 Gln221, not Leu. Correct fix: either B -> Q (restoring alignment to WNT3A 203-222) or, preferably, replace the whole peptide with the genuine WNT3A 203-222 segment CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP. Note the platform also has G at position 18 for WNT3A Ser220 and L at position 20 for Pro222, so three substitutions plus the illegal B, not the two the report implies. Second correction: 'it breaks the platform's one genuinely functional external integration' is not accurate — index.html:363 is a plain anchor to alphafoldserver.com that submits nothing, and copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) only writes to the clipboard. Nothing programmatic breaks; the failure is that a user's manual paste would be rejected. The character validator and the render-gate in the rest of the fix are correct and sufficient.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: INCOMPLETE RESIDUE AUDIT DESPITE A CLAIM OF COMPLETENESS. The overall assessment states 'I verified every residue-level claim against the actual UniProt sequences' and explicitly lists FZD8 Q9H461 and SLC1A2 P43004 — yet reports no error in either, and no finding covers five further mismatched target sites that I found. EAAT2/SLC1A2 (app.js:362) 'Thr368, Lys490' -> P43004 368 = Leu, 490 = Ala (both wrong). FZD8 (app.js:174) 'Phe72, Tyr125, Asp99, Arg104' -> Q9H461 104 = Leu (F72/Y125/D99 correct). GluN2A (app.js:216 and 236) 'Glu201, Lys210' -> GRIN2A Q12879 201 = Gln, 210 = Phe (both wrong). TrkA (app.js:268) 'His312, Leu331' -> NTRK1 P04629 312 = Ser, 331 = Glu (both wrong). PAFR (app.js:32, app.js:382, README:34) 'His14, Tyr200' -> P25105 14 = Arg, 200 = Leu (both wrong; Phe174 is correct). For symmetry, uncredited correct sets I verified: TLR4 O00206 Arg264/Lys341/Glu439 all correct; LC3B Q9GZQ8 Phe52/Leu63 correct; ER-beta Q92731 Glu305/Arg346 correct; hERG Q12809 Tyr652/Phe656 correct (README:99). text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE ONE GENUINELY SOURCED PEPTIDE IS MISSED, AND SO IS ITS MECHANISTIC ERROR. app.js:225 'GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG' is an exact match to GSK3B P49841 residues 3-34 and genuinely contains Ser9 — the single most defensible sequence in the dataset, and a real concept (the GSK-3beta N-terminal pseudosubstrate). But the platform then attaches it to the wrong pocket: app.js:226 says 'GSK-3beta ATP Binding Pocket (Val135, Asp133, Lys85)'. The pseudosubstrate does not bind the ATP pocket; it occupies the phosphate-binding pocket formed by Arg96, Arg180 and Lys205 (all three confirmed as those residues in P49841), and it only does so when Ser9 is PHOSPHORYLATED. An unphosphorylated Ser9 peptide is not an inhibitor and cannot bind where the platform says it binds. This is a clean, checkable mechanism-of-action error in the reviewer's own discipline, entirely unaddressed.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO FINDING PINS THE ROOT FALSE CLAIM: THAT ALPHAFOLD3 WAS EVER RUN. index.html:42 renders a header badge reading 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected'; README:24 claims 'direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server'; README:111 claims 'Live AlphaFold Server Connection'; README:108 claims 'Real sequence-driven backbone topology parsing'. In fact index.html:363 is a static anchor that transmits nothing, copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) only writes to the clipboard, and every pLDDT, dG and CEI is a hardcoded literal in AF3_CANDIDATES (app.js:124-135) and FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA. The claim 'designed via AlphaFold3' (README:22, README:45) therefore describes a computation that was never performed anywhere in the codebase. This is the provenance claim from which every other finding descends, and it deserves its own BLOCKER rather than being distributed across MOLBIO-02 and MOLBIO-11.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE SYNTHETIC pLDDT CURVE CONTRADICTS THE pLDDT NUMBERS PRINTED BESIDE IT. app.js:791 computes score = 93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode % 5)*0.5, whose range is 89.0 to 99.0 for every sequence. Consequently the clamps at app.js:792-793 ('if (score > 100) score = 98.6; if (score < 70) score = 76') are unreachable dead code — direct internal evidence that the curve was never derived from a prediction and that the clamps were copied from a template. It also means the rendered profile cannot reproduce the per-drug pLDDT strings it sits next to (e.g. 97.0 for X3 at app.js:166 versus a curve that averages ~94). The reviewer notes the formula is synthetic but never observes that it is arithmetically inconsistent with the platform's own headline confidence values.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: B4 IS BUILT FROM THE AMYLOID NUCLEATION MOTIF AND SOLD AS A FIBRIL DISRUPTOR. app.js:275-282 names B4 'AChE-Abeta Fibril Disruptor' with safety 'Fibril Blockade: 100%', and its peptide is Abeta16-35 (KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, verified as an exact APP P05067 substring) fused to GRLVGHPW. KLVFFAE is the self-recognition element that nucleates aggregation; unmodified Abeta16-35 is a seed, not a breaker. Genuine beta-sheet breakers require backbone N-methylation or proline substitution to abolish hydrogen-bonding on one face. The reviewer credits the sequence as 'the correct self-recognition element' and stops there, missing that using it unmodified inverts the stated pharmacology — the same class of error as MOLBIO-04, in a candidate MOLBIO-04 proposes to keep.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO ASSESSMENT OF WHETHER ANY OF THESE MOLECULES COULD REACH THE BRAIN, OR OF CATIONIC-PEPTIDE LIABILITY. Every one of the 25 candidates is a 28-47 residue peptide conjugate, and the ADMET section (README:96-102) addresses hERG, seizure index, cytokine storm and receptor downregulation while omitting the properties that actually disqualify this modality: blood-brain-barrier penetration, plasma and CSF proteolytic stability, and renal clearance. More specifically, the recurring 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (net +9, 4 Trp, amphipathic) is architecturally a cationic amphipathic cell-penetrating/antimicrobial peptide — a class that is membrane-lytic and haemolytic in the low-micromolar range. Asserting 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Risk)' for such a sequence while saying nothing about membrane lysis inverts the actual safety hierarchy for this chemotype. This is a first-order neuropharmacology omission the reviewer does not raise anywhere.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE 'TOLERANCE' AND 'BIASED AGONISM' CLAIM IS INCOHERENT FOR MOST OF THE PIPELINE'S TARGETS. README:102 states 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' because 'Biased agonist signaling redirects receptors to recycling endosomes.' Biased agonism is defined only for GPCRs (and by extension some RTK/cytokine systems). The pipeline's targets are dominated by a hydrolase (AChE), a ligand-gated ion channel (alpha-7), an ionotropic glutamate receptor (GluN2A), a secondary-active transporter (EAAT2/SLC1A2) and a Cul3 substrate adaptor (Keap1), none of which internalises or desensitises by the mechanism invoked. The reviewer flags desensitisation only for P1 in MOLBIO-06 and does not challenge the platform-wide mechanistic claim behind the number.
